**Lhotse** ([Nepali](Nepali_language "Nepali language"): ल्होत्से **L'hōtsē** Nepali pronunciation: [lot.se]; [Tibetan](Tibetan_script "Tibetan script"):  ལྷོ་རྩེ Tibetan pronunciation: [l̥otse], *lho tse*, [Chinese](Chinese_language "Chinese language"): 洛子峰) is the [fourth highest mountain](List_of_highest_mountains "List of highest mountains") in the world at 8,516 metres (27,940 ft), after [Mount Everest](Mount_Everest "Mount Everest"), <K2>, and <Kangchenjunga>. The main summit is on the border between [Tibet Autonomous Region](Tibet_Autonomous_Region "Tibet Autonomous Region") of <China> and the <Khumbu> region of <Nepal>.

With Everest to the north and <Nuptse> to the west, Lhotse forms the apex of the massive horseshoe-shaped arc of the Everest massif. Despite the tremendous vertical relief of its South and Northeast Faces, it is the least prominent of the eight-thousanders due to the great height of the [South Col](South_Col "South Col") between it and Everest. Lhotse's Western Face, recessed behind the head of the [Khumbu Glacier](Khumbu_Glacier "Khumbu Glacier") in the [Western Cwm](Western_Cwm "Western Cwm"), plays an integral part in the standard routes of ascent for both peaks; the name Lhotse, which means "South Peak" in [Tibetan](Tibetic_languages "Tibetic languages"), further emphasizes the close relationship between the two.

The main ridge of the mountain features four distinct summits: Lhotse Main at 8,516 metres (27,940 ft) above sea level, [Lhotse Middle](Lhotse_Middle "Lhotse Middle") (also known as Lhotse Central I or Lhotse East) at 8,414 m (27,605 ft), Lhotse Central II at 8,372 m (27,467 ft) and [Lhotse Shar](Lhotse_Shar "Lhotse Shar") at 8,383 m (27,503 ft). Though Lhotse Main is considered to be an intermediately difficult eight-thousander when ascended from the standard Reiss Couloir route, its secondary summits and extremely steep South Face are regarded as some of the most difficult and dangerous climbs in the world.[[2]](Lhotse#cite_note-Lhot_FAQ-3)[[3]](Lhotse#cite_note-K2_News-4)
